notes: Chromium background hosts: traffic the browser sends for itself, not for the page. scrapescope calls tunnel bytes 'background' ONLY when the host matches an entry here; an uncatalogued host is never called background. Every host has its own evidence in host_evidence (a source that names that host); evidence lists every source an entry uses, and credits name people or reports whose URL is in evidence. Hosts too broad to catalogue (www.google.com, which also serves /dl/ downloads per Google's documentation) are left out. Evidence URLs were last reviewed on the entry's last_verified date; re-check them before each release.

entries.component: Chromium optimization guide: hint fetches and on-device model downloads (tens of MB for a fresh profile)
credits: NodeMaven, measured 2026-08-19 (published by 2026-08-25): about 43 MB of optimization-guide downloads in a fresh browser profile through a proxy (intermittent: NodeMaven saw it in some idle windows, not all), not stopped by --disable-background-networking or --disable-component-update, removed by refusing the host at their relay
Skyvern postmortem (discussed on Hacker News, item 41593410): about 200 GB of proxy traffic in six hours; fixed with a persistent user_data_dir and a proxy rule rejecting this host
entries.security_tradeoff: Blocking it stops optimization-guide hint fetches and model downloads; browser features that rely on those hints and models may stop working or degrade, and which features use them varies by Chrome version. Certificate-revocation and Safe Browsing data arrive through other catalogued hosts.

entries.component: Chromium component updater and Chrome update downloads: update checks (update.googleapis.com) and component, CRX and update downloads (*.gvt1.com, dl.google.com)
entries.security_tradeoff: Component updates also deliver certificate-revocation data (CRLSet), Safe Browsing and other security components; blocking them leaves a long-lived profile with stale security data.

entries.component: Chrome extension update checks and .crx downloads (clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx, clients2.googleusercontent.com/crx/blobs), plus network-time queries on clients2.google.com
entries.security_tradeoff: Blocking it stops extension and component updates delivered through these hosts, including security fixes, and the network-time check Chrome uses to explain certificate date errors.

entries.component: Safe Browsing list updates and hash-prefix lookups
entries.security_tradeoff: Blocking it removes malware and phishing warnings from the profile; keep it for any browser that visits untrusted pages while signed in to real accounts.
